correctness.rationale: Independently checked the all-size proof. A type of minimum distance j is determined by its nearest E_j-class C: relative to any a in C its distance vector is x ↦ max(j,d(a,x)). These are valid finite extensions, and each has infinitely many realizations by extending with mutual distance one. For two distinct types with nested clusters, an old point in the smaller cluster forces the larger level as mutual distance; inside the larger cluster one distance is that level, and outside it the two old distances agree. For disjoint clusters the old intercluster distance exceeds both levels and is forced, with the remaining triangle inequalities following from the old ultrametric. For equal types the feasible distances are exactly 1 through their minimum level. This gives M_1=I, isolated units above s, and for each E_s-class a looped anchor and one zero-entry family per E_{s-1} child. Differences within each family are radical. Subtracting the anchor from one representative per child gives mutually orthogonal vectors of norm -1, each orthogonal to the anchor of norm 1. These are elementary integral basis changes, proving the stated congruence and all the Smith, rank and inertia consequences, including r=1. An independent r=3, two-point base at distance 2 gives M_2 congruent to diag(1,-1,-1,1).
residual_risks: The recorded finite census of 638 bases and 112842 entries is not the proof for arbitrary base size; the independent argument above supplies that proof. No formal verification is inferred.

value.rationale: Exact-distance compatibility on logical types over a named base is a natural finite invariant. The all-size integral result rules out torsion and rank drops in every characteristic and the signed form recovers the threshold partition counts; this information is not supplied by the usual existence of a ball tree or by one illustrative matrix.
residual_risks: The per-level congruence invariants do not recover the full old-point tree, nor do they determine the ordinary eigenvalues.
